literal: Fault being without, family having promoted, him who lives, as kindred will surround the world.
translation: The world will surround as its own kindred the man who lives without fault and elevates his family.
modern: எந்தக் குற்றமும் இல்லாதவனாய், தன் குடியை உயர்த்தி வாழ்கின்றவனை, இந்த உலகத்தார் தங்கள் சுற்றமாக ஏற்றுச் சூழ்ந்து கொள்வார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet describes the social reward for a person who leads a blameless life while working to uplift their family. The phrase 'குடி செய்து' (kuṭi ceytu) literally means 'having done family', which in this context means acting to build up or promote one's lineage. When a person lives without fault ('குற்றம் இலனாய்') and achieves this, the world ('உலகு') does not merely admire them from afar. Instead, it embraces and surrounds ('சுற்றும்') them as if they were its own kindred ('சுற்றமா'). The poetic repetition of the root 'சுற்று' (meaning both 'kindred' and 'to surround') emphasizes the close, familial bond society forms with such noble individuals.
